name: ULTRAKILL
creator: New Blood Interactive
desc: I really love ULTRAKILL, I got it around December of 2025 and I was instantly hooked, the main thing i love about it is the themings behind the game, ULTRAKILL and a lot of other media is based off the Divine Comedy - Dante's Inferno, which dictates the journey of Dante and his guide Vergil into the 9 layers of hell etc. ULTRAKILL flawlessly integrates a lot of the mythology into its game but twists it in its own way in such a perfect way. After playing it I really wanted to add my own interpretation to such media, So i made Inflerna which is now my largest project to date where i integrate Dante's Inferno in my own way, Another part of ULTRAKILL i love and am now integrating into my own media is the integration of a story driven loop and heavy replayability, because you first progress through ULTRAKILL's story but you can 'P' rank levels which means getting them perfect which adds hundreds of hours of replayability, and I also plan to use story driven + replayable mechanics in Inflerna

name: Library of Ruina
creator: Project Moon
desc: Library of Ruina is  such a cool game, my friend got me into it a few months ago and this game completely reshaped how i view deckbuilders, because unlike your typical deckbuilder, Project Moon created a riveting story based game where you customise 'Librarians' with Key pages that dictate their attributes like health speed etc. As well as that you can apply attack pages to them to further customise the moves they can use, these combinations of customisability allow for some insane builds and combos to be created. From this ive basically stolen the base ideas of it and changed to combat to be in my own light for Inflerna where flowers can be equiped with deeds and those deeds can have attack pages. As well as the deckbuilding, Library of Ruina has some insane writing and worldbuilding, and the techniques that are used I will be reviewing and 'Politely snatching' for enhancing my own storytelling inside of Inflerna

name: Balatro
creator: LocalThunk
desc: I was obsessed with Balatro since the day my friend gifted it to me, this game completely revamped my ideology of creating games and helped me to create one of my favourite approaches to game development, I call it the static camera, which basically means for the majority of the game the camera is static  or tends to move left down up or right respectively to different areas, this approach can be seen in many of my different games such as but not limited to, Inflerna, Mjefgee and Anathema, something about having different areas and static points the camera moves to really resonates with me. Another phillosophy I love and steal about Balatro is the intensive polish added to the game, such as lots of rotations, sound effect, growing on hover and many diffent things, I also loosely used the tabletop aesthetic in Anathema's development and Mjefgee too.

name: Terraria
creator: Re-Logic
desc: I first played Terraria years ago at this point and the phillosophy of ho the game works has heavilly impacted my game design choices, for one the way the 2D world generates I have studied, recreated and learnt from how it works, and the structuring of a side scrolling game in general I have learnt a lot from Terraria. Another thing I love Terraria for is how they do their bosses in a 2D sandbox, mainly focusing on more 'Bullet Hell' style gameplay but they make it work really well. A lot of mechanics from Terraria I ended up taking inspiration from and putting into one of my games called Honni. Another factor that I love about Terraria specifically is it started out as a small indie game and is now one of the most popular games of all time, indie successes give me a lot of hope for my own projects and inspire me to keep making things.
